questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Assess ability to design a modular, runtime-configurable data pipeline with per-tenant customization.

## Key Concepts
- Plugin architecture and the Pipeline pattern
- Immutable pipelines and copy-on-write config
- Per-tenant routing and hot-reload
- Stateless transforms and fault tolerance

## Code Example
```javascript
class Transform { constructor(name){this.name=name} apply(rec){return rec}}
class NormalizeTransform extends Transform { apply(r){ /* normalize */ return r} }
class Pipeline { constructor(steps){ this.steps=Object.freeze(steps)} process(r){ return this.steps.reduce((acc,t)=>t.apply(acc), r) } }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test per-tenant hot reload without downtime?
- How do you handle a failing plugin without aborting the whole record?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates the ability to design for runtime extensibility and reliability in a pluggable notification system.

## Key Concepts

- **Registry-driven plugins**: Channels are registered at runtime via a central registry, enabling new channel types without recompiling the core dispatcher.
- **Channel interface and factories**: A standardized contract ensures all notification channels implement common behavior while factories handle instantiation.
- **Per-user preferences**: Respect individual user settings for preferred notification channels and delivery priority.
- **Fallback strategy**: A reliable rollback mechanism ensures notifications are delivered even when primary channels fail.

## Why This Is Asked

Practical multi-tenant routing with runtime extensibility; assesses patterns and trade-offs.

## Key Concepts

- Strategy: channel dispatch per policy
- Registry: per-tenant policy storage
- Composite: policy groups with priorities
- Backpressure: async dispatch and rate limits

## Code Example

```javascript
// Interfaces sketch (simplified)
interface Channel { send(payload: any): Promise<void> }
interface Policy { evaluate(event: any): boolean; channels: string[]; priority: number }
interface PolicyRegistry { register(tenant: string, p: Policy): void; resolve(tenant: string, event: any): Policy[] }
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you ensure isolation across tenants during policy updates?
- How would you test performance under burst traffic?

## Why This Is Asked
Evaluates plugin architecture, isolation, and runtime extensibility in CLI tooling.

## Key Concepts
- Command pattern in plugins
- Runtime registry with versioning
- Sandboxed loading and security
- Hot reload and fallback semantics

## Code Example
```javascript
export interface Command {
  name: string;
  description: string;
  execute(args: string[]): Promise<number>;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle dependency conflicts and plugin sandboxing security concerns?
- What metrics would you collect to monitor plugin health and performance?

Provide interfaces, a TypeScript usage example, and discuss trade-offs?
